summary: Configured a persistent three-member MariaDB 10.11 Galera cluster. All members are Primary, Synced, Ready, and connected at cluster size 3. Multi-member writes, single-member availability, automatic resynchronization, and rolling reboot persistence were verified.
actions_performed: Installed MariaDB Server, Galera 4, and rsync on node1-node3.
Configured fixed Galera member addresses, InnoDB/ROW settings, rsync SST, recoverable gcache, network-online ordering, and enabled MariaDB at boot.
Verified writes through every member replicate to every other member.
Stopped node3, confirmed node1/node2 remained writable with quorum, then restored node3 and verified it automatically synchronized the missed write.
Restarted node1, node2, and node3 individually, waiting for full cluster recovery between restarts.
Performed final post-restart writes through all three members and confirmed identical data on every node.

evidence.summary: All three members report cluster size 3, Primary, Connected, Synced, Ready, active/enabled MariaDB, and listeners on ports 3306 and 4567.

evidence.requirement: Writes through any member replicate across the cluster
evidence.summary: Post-restart writes were accepted independently by node1, node2, and node3; every member subsequently returned the same seven rows.

evidence.requirement: Database remains available when one member is unavailable
evidence.summary: With node3 inactive, node1 and node2 remained Primary, Synced, Ready, and writable at cluster size 2; the outage-time write replicated between them.
After node3 returned, it automatically reached cluster size 3, Primary, Synced, Ready and contained the row committed during its absence.
